review.title: Production authentication and session resolution
review.acceptance: A request in a DEPLOYMENT can be identified, so that an account identity is never a typed header. This task owns the residual gpt-architect named when approving PW-0402, verbatim: PW-0402 does NOT establish production user authentication, and today a desktop build classifying as non-deployment would make the header the identity layer, with nothing currently preventing that classification. THE BOUNDARIES, WHICH THIS TASK DOES NOT MOVE. PW-0101 owns local listener authentication and hardening. PW-0402 owns authorization once an identity is known. PW-0401 owns the authenticated backend service for provider resolution. PW-0403 owns production account and session authentication and nothing else. REQUIRED: ADOPT the reviewed @liberty/auth/server Better Auth seam rather than replacing it. packages/auth/src/better-auth.ts is already the only module in the repository that imports better-auth, it already refuses a surface beyond ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES, and config.ts already validates secure-cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour. This task constructs the reviewed instance from that validated config; it does not stand up a second identity system beside it. REQUIRED: expose the Next App Router auth handler and endpoints, importing better-auth/next-js in apps/web rather than in the package, which must stay buildable and testable without Next -- the boundary better-auth.ts states in its own header. REQUIRED: a deployment request resolves AccountIdentity ONLY from a verified database-backed session. resolveRequestAccount gains a real deployment-authenticated branch instead of answering authentication_not_configured. REQUIRED: development headers stay strictly confined to a minted non-deployment runtime capability. The witness discipline in apps/web/src/lib/session/account.ts is preserved exactly -- a deployment cannot obtain an identity there, cannot be issued the witness, and a manufactured one is refused rather than accepted on the strength of its type. REQUIRED: a missing, malformed, expired or revoked session CANNOT produce an AccountIdentity. Each of the four is its own test, because 'expired' and 'revoked' fail through different code paths and a suite that covers only the missing case proves the least interesting one. REQUIRED: the desktop launch token cannot substitute for a user session. This is the exact confusion PW-0402's authorizeRoute was built to prevent by never being given a Request, and authentication must not reintroduce it from the other side. REQUIRED: a loopback origin cannot substitute for a user session. Being on 127.0.0.1 is not an identity. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE authentication and is not moved into Better Auth user or session product data. active_profile_selection is keyed by session in Liberty's own store, which is what lets the television and the phone act as different profiles; folding it into the identity library's session record would couple the two and lose that. REQUIRED: PW-0402's indistinguishable authorization refusal behaviour is preserved. An unauthenticated request and a request for another household's resource must not become distinguishable because one of them now fails earlier. REQUIRED: secure cookie, trusted-origin and baseURL behaviour comes from the existing validated auth configuration rather than from new literals at the handler. REQUIRED: no credential or secret is placed in the desktop artifact or in any log. REQUIRED: docs/SECURITY.md R4 is updated to state what is then true. Its current text was corrected in round 82 to say authorization is enforced and authentication is not; leaving that in place after this task ships would be a second competing truth.
review.notes: Filed in round 83 to own the residual gpt-architect named when approving PW-0402; acceptance rewritten in the same round to the reviewer's own round-83 specification, which is narrower and sharper than the original filing. allowedPaths gained apps/web/src/app/api/auth/** because Better Auth's validated basePath is /api/auth and the App Router handler has to live at the path the config already declares, not at a v1 path chosen to fit an earlier surface guess. The three packages/auth modules briefly added as reviewDependencies were removed again: packages/auth/src/** is already in allowedPaths and ai:validate correctly reported them redundant, because allowedPaths is always part of the reviewed surface.

typecheck.evidence: EXECUTED on da94ef4. npm run typecheck at the root, own invocation, turbo 21/21, exit 0. npm run lint 11/11 with zero problems and zero warnings. npx turbo run build --force 11/11, apps/web compiled successfully, and /api/auth/[...all] appears in the emitted route manifest as a dynamic entry, which is what export const dynamic = force-dynamic asks for. THE COMPILE-TIME LINKS DID THEIR JOB AND ARE WORTH RECORDING AS EVIDENCE RATHER THAN AS FRICTION: adding not_authenticated to RequestAccountRefusalReason broke the build in exactly the four places the design intends -- accountRefusalCode in db/request-context.ts, which widens the union by identity, and the three route groups' contract.ts widening functions. Each is an identity function whose only job is to fail to compile when a code is missing downstream, and none of them can be satisfied by a cast. Nothing was silenced; the vocabulary was extended in all four and in docs/API_CONTRACTS.md, which product invariant 5 requires. resolveRequestAccount becoming async broke exactly one production call site, resolveRequestContext, which was already async, so the whole cost was one await.

unit.evidence: EXECUTED on da94ef4. cd apps/web && npx vitest run over the three suites -> account 19, deployment-session 21, auth-instance 12, exit 0; monorepo npx turbo run test --force -> 20/20 packages, exit 0, apps/web at 1109 tests, up from 1075, every other package unchanged. NO POSTGRESQL AND NO AUTH LIBRARY IS NEEDED BY ANY OF THEM, which is a design property rather than a convenience: deploymentSessionAccount takes the session reader as an argument and selectAuthInstance takes every input explicitly, the same shape selectRepository already uses, so no suite mutates process.env and none races another in the same worker. WHAT THE 52 TESTS DEFEND. THE FOUR SESSION FAILURES ARE ONE ANSWER: absent, absent-spelled-undefined, malformed, expired and revoked are each a named case, each asserted to produce not_authenticated with one identical detail, and a further test collects the details into a Set and requires its size to be exactly 1 -- so the wordings cannot drift apart into four answers that can be told apart. That is the non-oracle discipline PW-0402's review required preserved, applied on the authentication side. WHAT CANNOT SUBSTITUTE FOR A SESSION is asserted as three ABSENCES, which is the only form that stays true when somebody later adds a header read for the desktop case: a request carrying both an Authorization bearer and an x-liberty-desktop-token is refused, a request from 127.0.0.1 with matching origin, host and x-forwarded-for is refused, and a request carrying both development headers is refused. A fourth test states it positively: the reader is handed request.headers BY IDENTITY and the function has no other channel into the request, so a later edit that passed the URL or the body fails. A SESSION THAT IS PRESENT BUT UNUSABLE IS NOT AN IDENTITY: six cases -- no user, no session, empty user id, empty session id, non-string id, null user -- all fail CLOSED as not_authenticated rather than as a server error. The empty-string cases are the reason the check exists: an empty id compares EQUAL to another empty id, so a defect upstream would silently merge households rather than fail. NEITHER ID REACHES THE TRAIL, asserted directly, because a session id in a log aggregator is a credential-shaped value and an account id is the one profileViewSchema already refuses to publish. THE STORE FAILING IS NOT THE VIEWER BEING SIGNED OUT: a thrown read reports authentication_not_configured, not not_authenticated, because retry-later is true of one and false of the other, and a thrown non-Error is asserted not to put the word undefined on the screen. THE COMPOSITION ROOT IS TESTED ONLY ON ITS REFUSALS, and that is deliberate -- constructing the instance needs a real Drizzle handle over a real pool, and a stub of one is a stub of Better Auth's constructor, which is the argument better-auth.ts itself makes for having no unit tests. The refusals are the part that decides whether a misconfigured deployment fails safe: the store is checked BEFORE configuration so an operator with no DATABASE_URL is not sent to fix a secret first; the in-memory adapter is refused outright; a PostgreSQL store with no connection string supplied is refused as two different reads of the environment; a short secret is refused, which is the dangerous class because a 12-character secret produces a WORKING system with forgeable cookies; a wildcard trusted origin is refused because the schema requires a URL; every problem is reported at once; and a refusal is asserted to contain neither the secret nor the password from the connection string. TWO SOURCE-LEVEL RULES: every process.env read is inside a function body, so the answer is not frozen to whatever the process looked like when the first route loaded, and the module contains exactly ONE throw -- the mail transport's, which is a rejected promise at send time -- with the count asserted rather than the keyword forbidden, because a ban would be relaxed the first time somebody adds a legitimate one and would then mean nothing. The mail placeholder is asserted to contain no console. and no message.url, because the two wrong defaults createLibertyAuth names are dropping the mail silently and logging a one-click account-takeover link.

e2e.evidence: EXECUTED Playwright runs at da94ef4, both modes, PLUS a live witness against a REAL POSTGRESQL, which is the part of this evidence that matters. Regression first: production npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium -> 73 tests, 61 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed; development LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development -> 73 tests, 70 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed. Both counts identical to the round-83 and round-84 runs, which is the wrap evidence: resolveRequestAccount became async and the account reason vocabulary gained a member, and nothing that existed behaves differently. THE LIVE WITNESS, and it is not a spec reading itself. PostgreSQL 16 was installed in this container, initdb'd on port 55432, and migrated with the repository's own packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql -- all eight tables including Better Auth's user, session, account and verification, which is the single first migration PL-0402 required rather than a retrofit. A PRODUCTION build was then started with DATABASE_URL, LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET and LIBERTY_AUTH_BASE_URL set, so the runtime classified as a deployment and took the branch this task exists for. Observed, in order: (1) GET /api/v1/profiles with no cookie -> HTTP 401, outcome refused, primary reason not_authenticated, with served_by_postgres_adapter beside it. That is the residual closed, measured. (2) The same request carrying x-liberty-development-account: household-b -> still 401. The development header does not authenticate a deployment. (3) POST /api/auth/sign-up/email -> 200 with a minted user id; the endpoint is served by the vendor instance at the path libertyAuthConfigSchema.baseUrl builds cookies for. (4) The resulting cookie -> GET profiles 200 outcome listed, and POST profiles 200 outcome created with a real uuid. An authenticated account can act. (5) REVOCATION, which is the whole justification for database sessions over stateless tokens: DELETE FROM session executed directly against the database, then the SAME cookie -> 401 not_authenticated on the very next request. No cache window, because createLibertyAuth declines Better Auth's cookieCache. (6) EXPIRY: a second account, UPDATE session SET expires_at = now() - interval '1 day', same cookie -> 401 with the identical detail. (7) TAMPERING: a hand-written cookie better-auth.session_token=forged.signature -> 401 with the identical detail. Cases 5, 6 and 7 are indistinguishable on the wire, which is the property the unit suite asserts and this confirms end to end. (8) With DATABASE_URL unset, GET /api/auth/get-session -> 503 naming the variable, and GET /api/v1/profiles -> 503 storage_not_configured. The endpoint exists and says the service behind it is not configured. WHAT THIS EVIDENCE DOES NOT COVER, stated rather than implied: there is no e2e SPEC for the authentication journey, because e2e/** is outside this task's allowedPaths and widening the surface to write one would be reservation inflation for a file the E2E lane owns -- the executed suites are regression evidence and the eight observations above are the feature evidence. No mail transport is configured, so verification and password-reset flows were not exercised and cannot be until one is; sign-up succeeded only because LIBERTY_AUTH_REQUIRE_EMAIL_VERIFICATION was set to false for the witness, and the default is true. The browser under test remains the unpinned revision for the reason PL-0704 recorded; only api and chromium ran; no claim is made about the CI job.

recommended.title: The authenticated backend the desktop build talks to
recommended.acceptance: The counterparty the desktop forwarder already speaks to exists as a service instead of only as an e2e stub. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 was ruled by the commander: provider resolution must not rely on the user-administered sidecar as its trust boundary, and the desktop build proxies to an authenticated backend. The FORWARDER is implemented and tested; the thing it forwards TO is e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. REQUIRED: the same route contract, byte for byte -- the cross-target e2e suite already compares whole bodies between targets and must keep passing. REQUIRED: caller authentication, and a refusal that does not leak whether a content id exists. REQUIRED: provider credentials live only here, never in a desktop artifact, env var, config file or cached response; the build-target import-graph guard already proves the desktop bundle cannot reach @liberty/provider-sdk and this service is where that capability actually lives. REQUIRED: it is deployable and testable WITHOUT a licensed provider -- the resolution path must return an honest unavailable with provider_not_configured when none is wired, which is exactly what the web target already does. THIS TASK DOES NOT NEED CREDENTIALS and must not wait for them; PL-0302 remains the separate task that wires a real provider into it.
recommended.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

recommended.title: A verdict that discusses the placeholder rule is not a placeholder
recommended.acceptance: A judgement gate's evidence can DISCUSS the rule that guards it without being refused by it. THE DEFECT, OBSERVED ON THE FIRST REAL USE OF PL-AI-0012 AND NOT PREDICTED. gpt-architect's round-84 verdict approving PL-AI-0012 lists, among its accepted properties, that filler wording does not become a valid judgement merely because the evidence is long -- and it names that wording using the very token the rejected-substring net matches. Transcribing the verdict faithfully was therefore REFUSED by the rule the verdict was approving. The gate was recorded with that one token reworded and the refusal disclosed in the evidence, which is a workaround and not a fix. THIS IS THE FIFTH TIME THIS REPOSITORY HAS PAID FOR THE SAME SHAPE, and that history is the argument for fixing it properly rather than trimming the word list: PL-0701's import guard failed on its own header comment naming the symbol it forbade; PW-0101's no-runtime-switch test failed on its own comment naming the environment variable; PW-0402 failed twice, once on an identifier that contained a forbidden word and once on a text window that reached into the code below it. Every one was a guard matching prose ABOUT the thing rather than the thing. REQUIRED: the rejected-substring net stops firing on a judgement that merely mentions the vocabulary. The implementer chooses the mechanism and must defend it; a shorter word list is NOT a defence, because the next verdict will discuss whichever words remain. The two shapes worth weighing are scoping the net by length -- a placeholding string is short by nature, and evidence long enough to argue about the rule is not one -- and exempting quoted or clearly-cited spans. Whatever is chosen, say in the module why the OTHER one was not. REQUIRED: the net keeps catching what it was built for. The round-83 string, and a real sha followed by wording that says the judgement has not been made yet, must both still be refused, and both already have regressions in scenario 10u that must stay green. REQUIRED: a new regression records THIS incident -- a long, faithful verdict that names the rejected vocabulary while approving a task, accepted; the short string that is nothing but that vocabulary, refused. REQUIRED: the commit-naming rule is untouched. It is the actual rule; the substring list is a second net and the policy note already says so. Nothing here may weaken the requirement that a verdict names the commit it judged. NOT IN SCOPE: the judgementCommitVerified behaviour, which gpt-architect approved as implemented in round 84 with an explicit instruction that it must not become a blanket refusal outside git.
recommended.notes: Filed in round 84 by claude-lead, immediately after PL-AI-0012 was approved and while recording that very approval. NOT one of the two defects gpt-architect ruled must stay inside PL-AI-0012 -- those are advance-completable self-attribution and the harness helper, both manifestations of the authority defect and both repaired there. This is a separate, newly observed defect in the second-net heuristic, found after the reviewed sha. It is filed rather than patched into PL-AI-0012 because that task is approved at 94dd10e and reopening an approved surface to refine a heuristic would invalidate a verdict for no safety gain. P2 because the workaround is a reworded token and the actual rule -- naming the commit judged -- is unaffected.
